resources.string: Build and manage your training programs
Browse and edit the exercise library
Programs, gyms and workout days open locked, so a drag handle cannot shuffle them by accident. Unlock from the padlock on each list.
Look back at and edit logged workouts
Body weight and measurements over time
No active program. Pick one to get workout suggestions here.
Ease back in with a rebuild program:

A program is a set of workout days, for example Push, Pull and Legs. Each day lists exercises with planned sets, target reps and rest times. Mark one program as active and the home screen suggests which day is next. You can keep several programs and switch whenever you like.

Start from the Home or Session tab: take the suggested day, pick another one, or begin an empty workout. While training, the set you are on is boxed in the accent colour - tap Done to complete it. The rest timer starts by itself, the keyboard gets out of the way, and the next set scrolls into the middle of the screen. In a superset the box alternates between the exercises. Finish ends the whole workout.

The Library tab gathers programs, exercises, gyms, workout history and body metrics. Skrot ships with a large exercise catalog, and the search matches English names, Swedish names, muscle groups and equipment all at once - with name hits first. Lists can be ordered alphabetically or by what you train most, from Settings. Create your own exercise, or clone an existing one and adjust it.

Statistics opens with a summary of the selected range — sessions, sets, volume, average length and your run of training weeks — then training frequency, muscle-group balance, volume per week, your most trained exercises and per-exercise charts with personal records. Body weight can be logged and followed here too. The list of logged workouts lives under Library → Workout history, where opening one lets you correct it with undo/redo, or delete it.

Everything is stored offline on your phone — no account, no cloud. Export a JSON backup from More → Backup and keep it somewhere safe; importing it restores everything, including on a new phone. Skrot reminds you when it is time; the interval is set in Settings.

Every exercise lists the equipment it needs, and every gym keeps a list of which exercises are available there. When you start a workout at a gym, unavailable exercises are swapped to an equivalent from the same exercise family, or you get to choose - and you can always search the whole library for something else. Whatever you pick, Skrot offers to remember it: mark it as available here, use it here from now on, or treat the two exercises as interchangeable everywhere.

Training somewhere that isn\'t one of your saved gyms - on holiday, at a hotel? Pick Temporary gym when starting. Skrot then assumes nothing is available and asks you to confirm every exercise, you can swap freely, and nothing is saved to your gym setups.

Changes made during a workout - adding or removing sets or exercises, reordering them, swapping one out, building a superset - apply to that session only. When something differs from the plan, a discreet \"Apply to future sessions\" button appears next to it. To write the whole shape of the session back at once - exercises, order, supersets, set counts - use \"Update program day\" in the workout menu. Ignore both and the plan stays untouched.

Exercises placed in the same block are run as a superset: while logging, the box alternates so you always see which set is next. Build one in the day editor, or during a workout with \"Add exercise to this block\" and \"Link with previous\"; \"Unlink\" splits one back out. Sets can also be marked as warm-up, drop or failure sets; warm-up sets are excluded from records, estimates and progression.

An exercise measures load as free weight, as a machine level, or as bodyweight with optional added weight. Machine levels aren\'t comparable between gyms, so history and charts for machine exercises are kept per gym. Bodyweight exercises use your logged body weight and a per-exercise factor when volume is estimated.

When you start a planned day, the sets are prefilled - from your last session or from the plan\'s targets, depending on the program\'s prefill mode. A set\'s target is the reps you need to reach for it to count: hit the target on every standard set at the same load, and the next session suggests more weight. The increment settings decide how big that step is, globally and per exercise.

Mark a gentler program as a recovery program in its editor. After a long break it is offered on Home and the Session tab, on the day of your choosing rather than always the first. Finish a recovery workout and the next one is offered straight away, continuing through that program, until you log an ordinary session again. The Session tab can keep the option permanently on hand.

More > Home screen chooses what the home screen shows. The next workout, recovery offers, a recap of your last session and your latest body metric are on by default. Days since your last workout, a run of training weeks and estimated 1RM for lifts you pick are there to switch on. The 1RM card tracks squat, bench and deadlift until you edit the list, and reads from your latest session, the past year, the past three years, or all time.

Programs, gyms, workout days, exercises within a session and the sets inside them can all be dragged into order by their handle. Lists open locked so a stray drag cannot shuffle them; the padlock unlocks the one you are looking at, and Settings decides whether they start locked. Sessions lock the same way, which also protects set and exercise structure while you train.

Switch on \"Plan exercises before starting\" in Settings and every routine workout runs through its exercise list first: how many sets and target reps each has, and how each stands at the gym you picked - available, swapped automatically, needing a choice, or missing. You can swap or skip from there before the first rep.
A session with no activity for the configured time is finished automatically, so a forgotten workout doesn\'t stay open. The threshold lives in Settings.
Everything here is optional and never leaves your device.

The program day will be rewritten to match this session: exercises, order, supersets and how many sets each exercise has. Rep targets and target loads are kept, and nothing you have logged today changes.
Session locked — only weight, reps and completing the active set can be changed.
Target hit last time — increase to %1$s?
Target hit last time — go for %1$d reps?
Built-in exercise — locked. Use the clone button above to make an editable copy.
Mark which exercises are available at each gym. Your routines stay gym-agnostic — Skrot swaps in equivalents when you train elsewhere.
On: edits to custom exercises, programs, workout days and gyms wait for Apply or Cancel. Off: changes stick immediately, like before. Built-in exercises are always locked either way.
Locked sessions block structural edits (sets, exercises, targets, rest); weight, reps and completing the active set always work. Toggle the padlock in a session to override.
Everything stays on your device. Export a full backup to a file, or a CSV of the workout log for spreadsheets.
Importing replaces ALL current data with the backup\'s content. This cannot be undone.
Import your programs and training history from a JEFIT CSV export. Exercise names are matched against the library; the rest become custom exercises.
Which unit does the JEFIT export use?
Imported %1$d sessions with %2$d sets. %3$d new exercises created.
No workout data found in the file.
%1$d body log entries will be imported.
Skrot is a free, open-source strength training log. No ads, no accounts, no cloud — your data stays on your device.
Gym icons from Tabler Icons (MIT), body icons from OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0), the rest from Material Symbols (Apache 2.0).
Skrot has no network permission — it is provably offline.
